name: Teodoro Paleologo di Montferrato
summary:
Teodoro Paleologo di Montferrato (1425–1484) was a Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop of the Diocese of Alessandria, playing a pivotal role in the Italian Renaissance.

As a diplomat for Pope Sixtus IV, he facilitated the signing of the Treaty of Ferrara with the Ottoman Empire in 1479, securing peace between Italy and the Middle East for nearly a century. This treaty not only showcased his diplomatic prowess but also marked a crucial turning point in the global balance of power.

As cardinal, Teodoro Paleologo di Montferrato was deeply involved in the conclave that elected Pope Innocent VIII in 1484, who subsequently launched the Inquisition against heretics. This event highlighted the increasing tensions between religious authority and secular power during this period.

Despite his significant contributions to diplomacy and religion, Teodoro Paleologo di Montferrato's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by other figures of the time. Nevertheless, his work as a cardinal and diplomat remains an important chapter in the history of the Italian Renaissance.

In 2019, archaeologists discovered a previously unknown chapel dedicated to Teodoro Paleologo di Montferrato within the Vatican Museums, featuring intricate frescoes that tell the story of his life and diplomatic achievements.
